newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BASLER DEFENDS HIMSELF AFTER VOGTS CRITICISM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BASLER DEFENDS HIMSELF AFTER VOGTS CRITICISM.

text.p: Germany midfielder Mario Basler on Wednesday defended himself against criticism of his fitness by coach Berti Vogts.
Vogts last week sent a letter to his players berating them for poor play since they won last year's European championship in England.

"That the national coach could not be satisfied with the 0-0 is obvious," the Bayern Munich player told the Sport Bild weekly, referring to Germany's draw with Ukraine in a World Cup qualifying game last month.

"But he also complained about my physical fitness, that I was only really fit for 60, 70 minutes. I can't just let that rest," he said. "Everything was great after we beat Ukraine 2-0 in the home game and three weeks later everything was wrong."
Basler scored the second goal in Germany's victory over Ukraine in May, but sustained a thigh strain during the match.
Criticism of the national side has grown louder during their World Cup qualifying campaign in which they have looked unimpressive and drawn three of their six games.
Basler said he wanted to talk to Vogts about his criticism before Germany face Northern Ireland on August 20 in their next World Cup qualifier.

Germany are second in group nine, two points behind Ukraine. But Vogts's team still have an excellent chance of winning the group as their opponents have failed to take advantage of their poor performances.
The group leaders have played two games more than Germany and third-placed Portugal are three points behind.
Basler also called on team mate Lothar Matthaeus to settle a row with other players at champions Bayern or risk the club's chances next season.
"We need every player and not one who is feeling insulted. That means: we must end these old rows and come together. Otherwise we have absolutely no chance of survival," he said.
